title: A bank account whose failures carry the numbers and change nothing

blocks.text: The page's `BankAccount` follows the best practices: exception names that say what went wrong, context carried in fields, and checks that run before any state changes. Write it.

items: Complete the checked `InsufficientFundsException(String message, double requestedAmount, double accountBalance)` with `getRequestedAmount()` and `getAccountBalance()`.
`deposit(double amount)`: an amount that is not positive (zero, negative, or `NaN`) throws `InvalidAmountException("Deposit amount must be positive")`;

`withdraw(double amount)`: an amount that is not positive throws `InvalidAmountException("Withdrawal amount must be positive")`; more than the balance throws `InsufficientFundsException("Insufficient funds for withdrawal", amount, balance)`.

blocks.text: Opening balances are never negative, so the two checks of `withdraw` never both apply; their order is up to you. How the exception stores its numbers is up to you as long as the getters return them.
A caller should be able to build a precise reply from the exception without parsing its message, and an account that refused an operation must be exactly as it was. Mind both ends of every range.

cases.says: Valid deposits and withdrawals change the balance.
A negative amount is an InvalidAmountException naming the operation.
InsufficientFundsException carries the requested amount and the balance, each in its own getter.
Every check runs before the balance changes, so a failed withdrawal leaves it as it was.
Zero is not a positive amount, for a deposit or a withdrawal.
Withdrawing exactly the balance is allowed and leaves 0.
NaN is not a positive amount: it is rejected instead of turning the balance into NaN.

concepts: A custom exception carries the data a handler needs in typed fields, not only in its message.
Validating before changing state leaves the object as it was when a method throws.
